discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 050704
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
204 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy drizzle and showers at times, especially this
  afternoon. Not as warm with highs only in the 50s. 

- Lake effect rain tonight through Friday, tapering off 
  Saturday morning. 

- Seasonably cold this weekend with highs in the 50s. Cold
  Sunday morning with lows near freezing. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 203 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

A 996mb low swirls over the UP this morning (bringing much needed 
rain to a drought-striken area), with a secondary shortwave trough 
aloft digging into extreme eastern Iowa. This has spawned a fairly 
widespread area of rain and drizzle upstream. This feature is 
still digging south-southeast this hour but is expected to lift 
northeast this afternoon. As it does so, scattered showers will 
move through for the afternoon. Remaining somewhat breezy once 
more with a modest pressure gradient still in play. Temperatures
only in the 50s today with only modest cold air advection noted
aloft due to boundary- parallel flow. However, a strong push of
CAA rushes in this evening/tonight as the primary trough axis 
(digging in through Minnesota this morning) sweeps through. This
CAA and lift promotes widespread showers followed by lake 
effect rain showers. If you're a snow lover, this is truly a 
waste of what would otherwise be an impressive lake effect snow 
set up. High resolution CAMS suggest QPF through the event 
of 0.30-0.50". Equilibrium levels crest at nearly 9,000 ft, 
indicative of excellent lake induced lift. A single band of 
rain is anticipated late Thursday night through Friday night 
that follows the eastern shore and wavers over La Porte and 
western St. Joseph (IN) counties. Lake effect comes to and end 
Saturday morning as equilibrium levels fall in response to 
rising heights aloft with the parent trough moving off. 

Compared to recent temperatures, very cold early Sunday morning in 
the wake of this system as skies clear and high pressure descends 
over the Great Lakes. Lows will be near freezing which is just shy 
of normal: 35 degrees. Over the course of next week, a classic sine 
wave pattern takes shape at 500mb with a towering Central US
ridge bookended by troughs. We'll be on the edge of seasonably 
cool northwest flow. If northwest flow wins out, we could see 
episodes of light rain (though Pacific moisture transport is 
poor). Alternatively, mild and dry conditions could prevail if 
the ridge to our west shifts east late in the week. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1228 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

In the wake of the cold front passage yesterday we will continue
to see mainly MVFR cigs with a few lower clouds and
sprinkles/drizzle at times through the overnight hours. Some
drier air does begin to push into the region by late morning 
and early afternoon which will allow for some improvement to
cigs but look to remain MVFR ahead of the next disturbance that
moves through from the northwest and spread southeast later 
tonight after 20z Thu. Westerly winds will back to more
northerly through the TAF period with gusts around 20kts
expected.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 PM EST this evening for LMZ043-
     046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Andersen

spc.text:
SPC AC 050551

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1151 PM CST Wed Nov 04 2026

   Valid 051200Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely today and tonight.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low over the Great Lakes is forecast to strengthen through
   the day today as it merges with a weaker shortwave trough emanating
   from the mid MS Valley. East of the mid-level cyclone, a belt of
   enhanced southerly flow aloft will gradually overspread portions of
   the Appalachians and Atlantic Seaboard into the evening and
   overnight hours. A broad surface low over the lower St Lawrence
   valley will weaken as a second low forms over the eastern Great
   Lakes. An associated diffuse cold front is forecast to move slowly
   southeastward across the Appalachians toward the Atlantic Coast.

   ...Carolinas to the Mid Atlantic...
   Ahead of the cold front a moist air mass will remain in place with
   dewpoints in the mid 60s F. Low-level warm air advection will favor
   cloudiness and only modest buoyancy with continued weak southerly
   surface winds. The stronger flow aloft is expected to arrive later
   in the diurnal cycle and will mainly be focused behind the cold
   front. Given the weak overall forcing and modest buoyancy,
   relatively isolated showers and thunderstorms are expected.
   Additional storms may develop along the front later in the evening,
   but little severe potential is expected owing to the weak buoyancy
   and poor overlap with stronger vertical shear.

   ...Southern New England...
   Farther north, a moist but cooler boundary layer will likely be in
   place ahead of the cold front from MA to southern NY. The humid
   environment could support very weak buoyancy immediately ahead of
   the front amid strengthening flow aloft. Frontal forcing is not
   expected to be overly strong, but could support a shallow convective
   band ahead of the front late in the evening and overnight. Some
   potential may exist for intermittent strong gusts to reach the
   surface, but confidence remains quite low.

   ...OK/TX...
   A weak vorticity max will move across OK on the southwestern flank
   of the larger-scale eastern trough. Cool mid-level temperatures will
   support weak elevated instability, with a few thunderstorms expected
   through the day and into the evening. Scattered elevated
   thunderstorms are also expected over Deep South TX, as the southern
   end of the cold front undercuts a moist air mass near the Gulf. Weak
   shear and buoyancy should preclude a severe risk.

   ..Lyons/Weinman.. 11/05/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 050644

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1244 AM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE EASTERN
   CAROLINAS AND FAR SOUTHEAST VIRGINIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few strong to severe storms are possible Friday over parts of the
   eastern Carolinas and southeast Virginia.

   ...Discussion...
   An upper low will move slowly east across the Great Lakes with a
   leading speed max farther east into the Mid Atlantic. Moderate
   southwest winds and cooling aloft will overspread that region during
   day, with a surface trough developing from southern New England into
   the eastern Carolinas.

   Ahead of a cold front, southwest low-level winds with 20-30 kt 850
   mb speeds will maintain mid 60s F dewpoints from eastern VA
   southward. Heating will be limited as rain and storms are likely to
   be ongoing Friday morning from southern New England into Virginia.
   Increasing large scale ascent will further expand storm coverage by
   midday into the Carolinas.

   A narrow plume of MLCAPE to 1000 J/kg is possible ahead of the
   ongoing activity/outflow, with effective shear of 35-40 kt. A few
   bowing structures may occur with locally damaging gust, or perhaps a
   brief tornado. However, the primary mitigating factor will be
   relatively poor low-level lapse rates.

   ..Jewell.. 11/05/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 050814

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0214 AM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are unlikely on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move across the northeastern states on Saturday
   with another shortwave aloft diving southeastward across the upper
   MS Valley. This will support cool conditions as high pressure
   settles into the MS/OH Valleys, with offshore winds across the Gulf
   and Atlantic coasts. High pressure will also exist across the Great
   Basin, behind an upper low dropping southeastward into Mexico. As
   such, little if any instability will be present to support
   thunderstorms over land.

   ..Jewell.. 11/05/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
